# Introduction

This project uses EPA air quality data from 2018 to 2020. I cleaned the data and made tables and plots for CO, PM2.5, and O3. The 2020 data only include January to April.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("project 2.R", local = TRUE)
```

# Data Cleaning

I wrote a function to clean the data. It removes duplicate rows, changes negative values to zero, and calculates daily averages. It can also change O3 units from ppm to ppb.

# Summary Tables

The tables show the minimum and maximum daily concentrations for each year.

```{r table2018}
knitr::kable(table2018,
             caption = "Daily Pollutant Concentrations in 2018")
```

```{r table2019}
knitr::kable(table2019,
             caption = "Daily Pollutant Concentrations in 2019")
```

```{r table2020}
knitr::kable(table2020,
             caption = "Daily Pollutant Concentrations in 2020")
```

# Visualizations

## Plot 1: CO and O3 by Month

This plot shows monthly averages and 95% confidence intervals using daily data from all available years.

```{r plot1, fig.width=7, fig.height=6.5}
print(plot1)
```

I used separate panels with different y-axis scales because CO and O3 have different concentration ranges. This makes both patterns easier to see.

## Plot 2: PM2.5 by Month and Year

```{r plot2, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
print(plot2)
```

I used lines and points to show monthly changes and compare the three years.

# Interpretation

CO was generally higher in winter, while O3 was higher in spring and summer. PM2.5 changed across months and years, but did not show a clear seasonal pattern. The 2020 data only cover four months, so comparisons are limited.

# AI Use Statement

I used ChatGPT to help to write and fix my code and improve the plots. I also used ChatGPT to generate an README.md and Rmd file to summarize the code. I checked the code and results in RStudio, including the tables, plots, duplicate dates, negative values, and unit conversion.
